title: SAME MODEL, BETTER PERFORMANCE: THE IMPACT OF SHUFFLING ON DNA LANGUAGE MODELS BENCHMARKING

bias_targets.methodology: Analyzing spurious performance variations and relative rankings of DNA language models (e.g., HyenaDNA, DNABERT-2, ResNet-LM) on genomic tasks when altering hardware-dependent data loading hyperparameters like the number of workers and buffer sizes.

Evaluating how the dependence of on-the-fly benchmark shuffling mechanisms on computational resources (such as memory for larger buffer sizes and CPU for parallel workers) skews comparative results in favor of researchers with access to superior infrastructure.
Demonstrating how fixed memory constraints interact with different model embedding sizes, disproportionately degrading the evaluation performance of larger models that require smaller buffer sizes.
